title: Life-cycle rules, versioning and retention policies

videos.script: Lesson 1 ended with a file overwritten for good. This lesson is about the ways to stop that, and what each one costs. {{undo}} The first is versioning. A versioned bucket keeps every generation it was given, and a delete only makes the live one noncurrent. You delete one, and bring it back with a copy. {{versions}} Keeping everything has a price. A table rewritten every night is a new full copy every night, and a short program shows a year of that adding up, with soft delete adding its own week. {{bill}} The second is a life-cycle rule, which moves old files to colder classes and deletes what nobody needs. The emulator accepts the rule and keeps none of it. {{rules}} The third is a retention policy, and once it is locked nobody can delete an object before its time, not even the project's owner. {{lock}} Here the emulator deletes the invoice anyway. And it does worse with versions: asked to delete an old one, it deletes the live one. {{weak}} You will see exactly where the imitation gives way, and what a test against it can still prove. {{end}}
